key_insight: A room-temperature methylammonium polybromide melt can directly convert elemental metal films into optoelectronic-grade bromide perovskites in a single, solvent-free step.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable, roll-to-roll compatible route to fabricate perovskite films from stable metals, reducing processing complexity and improving pathway flexibility for device manufacturing.
method: Use methylammonium polybromide melt as the reactive medium
Expose elemental metal films (Pb, Sn, Au, Cu) to PBM at room temperature
Tune PBM composition to control reactivity and suppress unwanted oxidation, especially for Sn
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful phase conversion to MAPbBr3, MASnBr3, MA2Au2Br6, and MA2CuBr4, with in situ XRD detecting transient intermediates in two cases and high-quality MASnBr3 films achieved under ambient conditions.
watch_item: Reaction outcomes depend on metal oxidation/disproportionation tendencies, so some systems may require careful PBM tuning to avoid overoxidation or incomplete conversion.
paper_title: A Universal Polybromide Melt Strategy for the Direct Conversion of Metals into Optoelectronic-Grade Bromide Perovskites
